newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally on Wall Street gains.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally on Wall Street gains.

text.p: Mexican shares recovered from a mid-session lull to close sharply highier for the second session in a row on Friday in the wake of a revival on Wall Street.
"Although it was a very speculative market, it did respond to advances by the Dow Jones," said Rodolfo Campuzano, an analyst at the Invex brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended up 51.46 points, or 1.35 percent, at 3,873.38. The Dow Jones Industrial average meanwhile closed up 32.92 points to 7,169.54.
Trading volume was lackluster at 70.6 million shares.
Dealers said that Telmex led the rally, buoyed by its ADRs and news it had obtained a $1 billion syndicated loan.
The telecomms firm's L class shares, which accounted for 17 percent of all shares traded, gained 30 centavos (4 cents) to 16.80 pesos ($2.12), while its ADRs ended up 1/2 at 42-1/8.
Financial group Bancomer was the most traded decliner, off 1 centavo (less than 1 cent) to 2.84 pesos (36 cents).
On the broad market, of 109 stocks traded, and gainers outnumbered sliders by 60 to 24.

Troubled Mexican conglomerate Sidek topped the percentage gainers' list for the third day in a row, up six centavos to 48 centavos, closely followed by its tourism subsidiary Situr, up two centavos (less than 1 cent) to 36 centavos (4 cents).

Hotel operator Posadas was also near the top of the gainers' list, up 25 centavos (3 cents) to 3.85 pesos (49 cents) on speculation the firm was to build a hotel on the site of a Mexico City racetrack, traders said.
